summary: Workspace deletion implemented with atomic storage, durable deleted-ID reservations, safe confirmation and client recovery. Verification uses only disposable data.

checks.title: Switch between project workspaces
checks.detail: r3: Deleted active projects open workspace selection; inactive deletion updates the selector while preserving the active editor. Last-project reload offers working create and archive import.

checks.title: Persist project data in durable workspace storage
checks.detail: r4: Atomic deletion and durable ID reservations persist through SQLite, D1 and PostgreSQL restarts. Deleted Asteroids seed data remains absent on index reads and initialization.

checks.title: Back up and transfer complete deployment data
checks.detail: r2: Administrative archives preserve minimal deletion records and same-actor retry results in every source/destination pair among SQLite, D1 and PostgreSQL. Deletion-only installations also restore without seed resurrection.

checks.title: Preview and atomically import complete workspace archives
checks.detail: r2: Deleted original IDs appear as reserved conflicts; restore is rejected and explicit copy creates a new ID with source provenance. Retrying an old import cannot resurrect a deleted destination.

checks.title: Confirm deletion of a project workspace
checks.detail: r1: Browser checks exercise duplicate names, exact-name gating, initial Cancel focus, cancellation, export success/failure, invalidation after a concurrent save, explicit local-input discard, pending confirmation and narrow-screen layout.

checks.title: Delete workspace data atomically and prevent recreation
checks.detail: r1: All three databases pass populated deletion, cross-project isolation, commit rollback injection, concurrent deletion replay, stale-write rejection and restart retry. Independent PostgreSQL processes race REST/MCP saves against deletion. Authorization, forged identity boundaries, Origin and input validation are checked.

checks.title: Recover navigation and editors after workspace deletion
checks.detail: r1: Two browser sessions detect deletion within five seconds and preserve remote pending input for explicit copying/discard. Deleted URLs and empty states recover without retargeting; sync tests reject late responses and stop deleted-project requests.

checks.title: Verify workspace deletion across supported deployments
checks.detail: r1: Disposable SQLite, Miniflare D1 and real PostgreSQL storage checks; separate production server processes; Chrome two-session UI checks; fault injection and a nine-pair backup transfer matrix passed. Exact execution scope and limits are listed below.

executions.scope: SQLite, Miniflare D1, PostgreSQL 17; populated records include Information, all proposal states, frozen snapshots, passing/failed evidence, history, guidance and implementation associations. All nine backup source/destination pairs verified.
Built production SQLite and separate PostgreSQL server processes; REST/MCP delete-versus-save races, retry, restart, authentication/revocation.
Chrome on macOS against built standalone SQLite; two browser sessions; 1280x720 and 390x844 views.

limits: D1 storage tests use Miniflare's D1 implementation; production customer workspaces were not deleted for testing.
Browser deletion workflow was exercised against standalone SQLite. PostgreSQL HTTP checks use independent server processes; D1 and PostgreSQL storage contracts are covered separately.
Sites build, deployment status and final source commit are recorded with BL-016 implementation and evidence metadata after publishing.
